Maria: quick dump from today's profiling run on TP=4 / model=rw-1.5b / seq=2048. seeing a weird step where all-reduce time jumps when KV-cache hits accumulate > ~24 tokens per request. attaching trace below.

Joe: can you paste the timeline? short snippet is fine.

Maria: sure — top-level summary first: ring allreduce dominates for mid-sized messages (~200KB-1.5MB) but tree wins for >1MB. small messages (<64KB) prefer ring. overall tail latency spikes on mixed-size microbatches.

Maria: trace: ```
# sample aggregates from perf profiler (ms)
step 1024: kv_serialize=3.2, allreduce_msg=1.9MB, nccl_ring_ms=18.6, nccl_tree_ms=10.2
step 1025: kv_serialize=2.8, allreduce_msg=56KB, nccl_ring_ms=1.3, nccl_tree_ms=1.9
step 1026: kv_serialize=4.1, allreduce_msg=840KB, nccl_ring_ms=11.0, nccl_tree_ms=6.7
# note: overlap fraction low (~10%) when kv cache merge is enabled across microbatches
```

Sachin: hmm. sounds like our batching heuristics + kv-cache merge are changing message-size distribution so ring isn't optimal. did you enable continuous batching?

Maria: yes, continuous batching on. microbatch coalescing policy is merging KV from consecutive requests when same routing key present — gives larger allreduce payloads.

Olivia: that matches a regression we saw in canary a week ago after the KV coalescing change. it improved throughput but increased median allreduce size. potentially causing worse comm/compute overlap.

Derek: quick thought: ring scales well for many small messages, tree better for fewer large messages due to shorter critical path. we should auto-select NCCL algorithm based on measured message_size threshold.

Joe: agreed. propose heuristic: if per-allreduce payload > 512KB -> prefer tree, else ring. also clamp max merged-kv-per-request to avoid pathological growth.

Maria: ran a quick experiment: switching NCCL_ALGO=tree for large msgs + split_kv_shards=2 reduced p99 by 38% on this workload, but p50 moved slightly up (~+6%). logs: ```
before: p99=512ms, p50=82ms
after: p99=318ms, p50=87ms
```

Sachin: OK tradeoff seems fine for latency-sensitive tenants. For throughput-first tenants we can keep current defaults. need an escape hatch config per-tenant.

Olivia: another angle: improve comm/compute overlap — kick off async allreduce earlier by emitting gradients as they arrive instead of waiting for full microbatch. that should hide some of the ring overhead.

Derek: +1. also kernel selection: check that large-reduction kernels are using the right reduce-scatter + allgather variants. I saw a fallback to non-optimized kernel in one trace (aligned sizes off by a factor).

Maria: tracked one kernel fallback — misaligned chunk size from our chunking heuristic. alignment fix + tree-algo switch removed that fallback.

perf-bot: experiment recorded: exp/1803502468/kv-coalesce-tree-switch. metrics: latency_p99, throughput, cpu_gpu_util. link: https://perf.internal/exp/1803502468 (internal). :rocket:

Joe: action items: 1) implement dynamic NCCL algo selector (owner: Joe, due EOD Wed) 2) add max_kv_merge cap (owner: Maria, due Thu) 3) prototype earlier async allreduce (owner: Derek + Sachin, due next week) 4) add kernel-alignment sanity check to compiler (owner: Olivia, due Fri).

Maria: I'll also add a small canary to Dedicated that flips the selector for a subset of capacity.

Olivia: nice. please attach the short reproducer script to the perf ticket.

Maria: done, added to exp ticket. closing the loop here — thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
